# What Comodor can do, and where each part lives

**Generated by `tools/capability-map.py`. Do not edit by hand.**

Regenerate after adding a command, a tool, a channel or a provider:

```
python tools/capability-map.py
python tools/capability-map.py --check   # fails if out of date
```

Git-ignored. This is a map of the machine for whoever is working on
it — `docs/` is what users read, and `PROJECT.md` is why the code is
shaped the way it is. This one answers *what exists and does it work*.

## The command line — 116 commands

Everything reachable from `comodor`. Sub-commands are indented under
the group that registers them.

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `acp` | run as an agent your editor can drive (Agent Client Protocol) |
| `approvals` | propose an allowlist from the commands you keep approving |
| `cron` | list, add, and manage scheduled jobs |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;`cron add` | create a job |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;`cron list` | show every job and when it next fires |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;`cron pause` | stop a job from firing |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;`cron remove` | delete a job |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;`cron resume` | start a paused job again |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;`cron run` | fire a job once, right now |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;`cron status` | whether the scheduler is enabled |
| `curator` | run, read, or steer the brain's maintenance pass |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;`curator pause` | stop the curator from running on its own |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;`curator pin` | exempt a skill from stale/archive |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;`curator report` | print the last pass's report |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;`curator restore` | bring an archived skill back |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;`curator resume` | let the curator run on its own again |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;`curator run` | do a pass now, regardless of the interval |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;`curator unpin` | let the curator curate a skill again |
| `discord` | drive Comodor from Discord |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;`discord connect` | save a bot token |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;`discord forget` | remove an account |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;`discord off` | switch it off without forgetting it |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;`discord pair` | add an account, with a one-time code |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;`discord service` | start it at login, so a reboot brings it back |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;`discord start` | run the bot |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;`discord status` | what is configured, and who may talk |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;`discord stop` | stop a bot running in the background |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;`discord writes` | whether a Discord turn may edit files and run commands |
| `doctor` | check everything, and repair what can be repaired |
| `help` | what this is and how to use it, in full |
| `import` | bring keys, model and skills over from another agent |
| `insights` | spend, activity and progress over recent days |
| `journey` | everything the brain has learned, oldest first |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;`journey remove` | retire one node, e.g. `remove rule:3` |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;`journey show` | the timeline (the default) |
| `local` | run a model on this machine, with no network |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;`local get` | download a model |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;`local list` | models you can run, and what is here |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;`local remove` | delete a downloaded model |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;`local use` | make a downloaded model the active one |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;`local where` | where the files are kept |
| `mcp` | connect Comodor to Model Context Protocol servers |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;`mcp add` | add a server from the catalogue |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;`mcp catalogue` | servers Comodor can set up for you |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;`mcp custom` | add any other MCP server by its command |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;`mcp disable` | turn a server off |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;`mcp enable` | turn a server on |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;`mcp list` | servers you have, and what they offer |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;`mcp prompt` | run a server's prompt template as your message |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;`mcp remote` | add a hosted MCP server by its URL |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;`mcp remove` | forget a server entirely |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;`mcp resources` | what the servers let you read, by URI |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;`mcp test` | start it and list its tools |
| `memory-provider` | point the brain at one external memory service (optional) |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;`memory-provider off` | forget the external service entirely |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;`memory-provider setup` | configure the service and test that it answers |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;`memory-provider status` | what is configured, and whether it answers |
| `plugins` | plugins: the user's own tools, hooks and commands |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;`plugins doctor` | why a plugin is not loading |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;`plugins list` | what is installed, and whether it loads |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;`plugins trust` | allow a project's plugins to load, after showing what a scan found |

| `preview` | render the interface at a given size and exit |
| `run` | run one task without the interface |

## What the agent may use

The mode decides. This is a registry built with nothing optional
attached, which is what a plain `comodor run` produces.

| Mode | Tools |
| --- | --- |
| `act` | `ask`, `browse`, `edit_file`, `glob`, `grep`, `list_dir`, `propose_mode`, `read_file`, `run_python`, `run_shell`, `todo_write`, `web_fetch`, `web_search`, `write_file` |
| `plan` | `ask`, `glob`, `grep`, `list_dir`, `propose_mode`, `read_file`, `todo_write` |
| `ask` | `ask`, `glob`, `grep`, `list_dir`, `propose_mode`, `read_file`, `todo_write` |
| `chat` | — none — |

### Only where something supplies them

These exist and are not in the list above. A registry built inside
a delegate or a scheduled run deliberately has fewer.

| Tool | Offered when |
| --- | --- |
| `browser` | `see tools/browser.py` |
| `computer` | `see tools/computer.py` |
| `cronjob` | `cron_store is not None` |
| `delegate` | `see tools/delegate.py` |
| `image_gen` | `config is not None` |
| `mcp_read_resource` | `mcp.has_resources()` |
| `memory` | `see tools/memory.py` |
| `read_skill_file` | `see tools/skills.py` |
| `search_history` | `see tools/history.py` |
| `skill_manage` | `see tools/skill_manage.py` |
| `vision` | `config is not None and getattr(config, "computer", None) \` |

## Channels — 4

| Channel | Panel form | Bot | CLI | Config |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Telegram | `token` | yes | yes | `TelegramConfig` |
| WhatsApp | `phone_number_id`, `token`, `app_secret`, `public_url` | yes | yes | `WhatsAppConfig` |
| Slack | `bot_token`, `app_token` | yes | yes | `SlackConfig` |
| Discord | `token` | yes | yes | `DiscordConfig` |

A channel with no panel form is one the web panel lists and cannot
connect — worth catching here rather than from a bug report.

## Configuration — 21 sections

`ui` `agent` `gateway` `learning` `curator` `skills` `safety` `browser` `computer` `telegram` `whatsapp` `slack` `discord` `cron` `media` `voice` `delegation` `shell` `api` `webhook` `image_gen`

Each is a dataclass in `config.py` and a block in `config.json`.
`load()` merges the user's file, then the project's `.comodor/`, then
the environment — see `PROJECT.md` for what a project file may not do.

## Does it run

Each of these was actually run while this file was written — not
`--help` on everything, which would prove only that argparse works,
but commands that reach into a subsystem and come back.

All 20 answered.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `comodor --version` | ok — exit 0 |
| `comodor --help` | ok — exit 0 |
| `comodor help` | ok — exit 0 |
| `comodor doctor` | ok — exit 1 |
| `comodor cron list` | ok — exit 0 |
| `comodor cron status` | ok — exit 0 |
| `comodor skills list` | ok — exit 0 |
| `comodor mcp list` | ok — exit 0 |
| `comodor telegram status` | ok — exit 0 |

| `comodor whatsapp status` | ok — exit 0 |
| `comodor discord status` | ok — exit 0 |
| `comodor curator report` | ok — exit 0 |
| `comodor insights` | ok — exit 0 |
| `comodor approvals` | ok — exit 0 |
| `comodor plugins list` | ok — exit 0 |
| `comodor local list` | ok — exit 0 |
| `comodor memory-provider status` | ok — exit 0 |
| `comodor journey` | ok — exit 0 |
| `comodor webhook list` | ok — exit 0 |

An exit code of 1 is not a failure here: `doctor` uses it to mean it
found something to report. A traceback always is.

## Test coverage

**2226 tests across 107 files.**

Run them with `pytest`. The parallel settings are in `pyproject.toml`,
and tests that measure wall-clock time are marked `performance` and
run separately — `pytest -m performance -n 0`.

### 8 modules no test file names

Not proof of no coverage — a module can be exercised through
another one — but each is worth a look.

- `comodor.__main__`
- `comodor._version`
- `comodor.api.session_map`
- `comodor.learning.journey_commands`
- `comodor.tools.todo`
- `comodor.ui.markdown`
- `comodor.ui.widgets.buttons`
- `comodor.ui.widgets.panel`
